uncited: *   **Definition:** A divergence-free vector field generated from noise derivatives, used to create smooth flow effects for particles.
Assume the vector field does not depend on vertical position ($z$), so $z$-derivatives are zero.
For a 2-channel curl output, assume the vector field only has a nonzero $F_z$ component.
The thesis describes constructing vector fields using mathematical descriptions to solve the initial value problem for point advection using Runge-Kutta integration.
Specific examples include Linear, ABC-Flow, and N-Force fields.
This work detailed the use of attractors to create breezes and wakes by defining radial paths with cosine falloff.

This method uses finite differences of noise textures to create divergence-free vector fields, optimized for 2D textures to reduce computational complexity while maintaining smooth flow characteristics.
